belief: People with money are better than me.
origins: Wealth often comes with confidence, polish, and access, and those can look like superiority. If we grew up with less, were treated as lesser, or were taught to defer to the wealthy, we may keep that stance for life. Media and workplaces can reinforce it by treating wealth as a measure of competence and worth.
teaches: Scripture says plainly that God does not show favoritism. Paul writes that there is neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, for we are all one in Christ Jesus. James asks, “Has not God chosen those who are poor in the eyes of the world to be rich in faith?” and Paul reminds us that God chose the weak things of the world to shame the strong. Before God, wealth does not rank people. We stand on level ground, with the same Maker and the same need of grace.
self_statements: They are smarter than I am.
I should defer to people with more.
I am not in their league.
I am less because I have less.
I should not speak up around them.
errors: Measuring my worth against someone’s wealth.
Assuming that wealth means they are better in every way.
Feeling small and concluding that I am small.
Seeing people as either high or low.
questions: What do I actually know about this person beyond their income?
Where did I learn to rank people by money?
What does God say about how He sees rich and poor?
What strengths and gifts do I have that money cannot buy?
How do I behave when I believe someone is “better” than me?
What would it look like to treat wealthy people as equals?
truth: God does not rank people by money. I am made in His image and loved by Him as much as anyone. I can respect others without bowing to them and can stand on the level ground Christ gives.
hw_truths: Money does not make a person better.
I am one in Christ with everyone.
I have gifts money cannot buy.
I can respect people without shrinking.
I stand on level ground before God.
log: Each week, write one situation in which you felt “less than” and one fact that corrects it.
actions: List five gifts or strengths you bring to any room.
In your next conversation with someone more wealthy, hold steady eye contact and speak as an equal.
Ask a question about their path, not just their position.
Say it each morning for a week.
prayer: Father, You show no favoritism. Free me from believing that people with money are better than I am. Help me see myself and others as You do, and to stand with humble confidence. Amen.
hw_questions: Where did I learn to rank people by money?
How does God see rich and poor?
How do I act when I feel “less than”?
What would equal footing look like?
What is one fact that corrects this belief?
name_example: Sarah can write: “We are all one in Christ, so I stand on level ground.”
